The pass that declines to overwrite it names it, and names something to run.

ticket.found_by: asking which OTHER writers destroy bytes in a home, after CHM-9/10/12 closed home sync
ticket.model_change: External gains ChildRefreshProvenance (SOURCE_AWARE / CONTENT_DIGEST_ONLY), the StoreOrigin token for a writer that is not a tier, and the action RefreshProjectChildHomeFromStore in the tier slice. That is what made the defect expressible at all: the unit slice's LocallyModified is content-based and so already forbade this, while the code's is record-based and did not. The defect lives in the difference, and the difference is only visible where records are.
ticket.objective: `home sync --merge` from a ticket worktree leaves the project home holding a tree that is PRISTINE BY ITS OWN RECORD -- the merge rewrote that record -- while being a wholesale copy of no store on earth. ChildHomeMaterializer.reconcile asks all three clauses of the baseline rule before it destroys anything: the destination still holds what its record says, the record is evidence about THIS source, and the tree is not a merge result. copyUnit -- the downward materialization that `project resolve` and `project sync` run -- asked only the first, and so did isLocallyModified, the predicate a prune, a teardown and a close-out consult before deleting. Consequence, reproduced end to end against the real CLI: resolve, clone the project home into a worktree, edit, `home sync --merge` back, `home close-out` clears, `rm -rf` the worktree, `project resolve` again. The ticket's bytes then existed in NO home, and the command that deleted them reported MATERIALIZED with the detail "copied from the parent store". No operator error is involved: it is the epic's documented flow with the ordinary dependency-refresh command run after it.
ticket.resolution: One reading of the rule, not three. ChildHomeMaterializer.Disposal is the whole conjunction as a value -- baseline, destUntouched, recordIsAboutThisSource, mergeResult -- computed once by disposal() and consumed by copyUnit, reconcile and isLocallyModified. The three inlined copies that disagreed are gone. linkUnit was brought under the same value: linkPath deletes a real directory to put a symlink where it stood, so a COPY child home somebody edited could be destroyed by a later pass that merely asked for LINK. The choke point is inside ChildHomeMaterializer rather than in Fs or in a new collaborator, and the reason is what evidence is available where: Fs knows nothing about homes or records, so a guard there would either have to be handed a baseline by every caller -- which is the same N call sites -- or invent provenance it cannot have.
